```{=html}
<div class="resource-page start-page">
  <section class="resource-hero" aria-labelledby="start-title">
    <div>
      <p class="eyebrow">STT-1100</p>
      <h1 id="start-title">Start the Course</h1>
      <p>STT-1100 works as a data science pathway. Each module begins with a concrete situation, places you in a professional role, and leads you to produce something visible: a report, an analysis, a visualization, a function or a dashboard.</p>
      <div class="resource-actions" aria-label="Quick access">
        <a class="home-action home-action--primary" href="modules.html">See modules</a>
        <a class="home-action" href="boite_outils.html">Toolkit</a>
        <a class="home-action" href="ressources.html">Resources</a>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="resource-panel" aria-label="Pathway markers">
      <div><span>01</span><p>Read the learning plan</p></div>
      <div><span>02</span><p>Enter the adventure</p></div>
      <div><span>03</span><p>Complete the challenge</p></div>
      <div><span>04</span><p>Consolidate with exercises</p></div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="philosophy-title">
    <div class="resource-section__header">
      <h2 id="philosophy-title">Course Philosophy</h2>
      <p>You learn data science by producing, explaining and revising your own work.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="principle-grid">
      <article class="principle-card">
        <h3>Understand before automating</h3>
        <p>Code is there to answer a question. Before looking for the perfect function, identify the variables, context, units and expected deliverable.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="principle-card">
        <h3>Work reproducibly</h3>
        <p>Quarto reports, R scripts and GitHub repositories keep the reasoning visible. A result should be reproducible, readable and explainable.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="principle-card">
        <h3>Build careful interpretations</h3>
        <p>A useful analysis is not just a chart or a model. It states what the data support and what they do not allow you to conclude.</p>
      </article>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="plan-title">
    <div class="resource-section__header">
      <h2 id="plan-title">How a Module Works</h2>
      <p>Each module home page presents the learning plan as expandable cards.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="course-flow">
      <article class="flow-card">
        <span class="flow-number">1</span>
        <h3>Readings</h3>
        <p>The readings give you the language, concepts and functions to recognize. They prepare the adventure; they do not replace practice.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="flow-card">
        <span class="flow-number">2</span>
        <h3>Adventure</h3>
        <p>The adventure is the main immersion. You play a data science role and follow a guided situation, often longer and more contextualized.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="flow-card">
        <span class="flow-number">3</span>
        <h3>Challenge</h3>
        <p>The challenge turns guided practice into a personal production. It is the short deliverable that shows what you can do in the module.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="flow-card">
        <span class="flow-number">4</span>
        <h3>Exercises</h3>
        <p>The exercises stabilize technical habits: importing, transforming, visualizing, diagnosing, interpreting and rendering work.</p>
      </article>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="immersion-title">
    <div class="resource-section__header">
      <h2 id="immersion-title">Data Science Immersion</h2>
      <p>The modules place you in the roles that structure a data science project. The goal is to learn technical gestures while understanding who produces, protects, analyzes and communicates data.</p>
    </div>
    <figure class="workflow-figure">
      <img src="autre_materiel/Présentation%20des%20différents%20rôles/whole-game.png" alt="Full data science project cycle: import, tidy, transform, visualize, model and communicate.">
    </figure>
    <div class="role-grid">
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Data Engineer</h3><p>Make reliable, accessible and well-structured data available by designing architectures, imports and automations.</p></article>
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Data Owner</h3><p>Guarantee data governance, compliance and quality: metadata, access, source, updates and privacy rules.</p></article>
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Statistician</h3><p>Model phenomena, quantify uncertainty and help distinguish what the data truly support.</p></article>
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Data Scientist</h3><p>Turn data into products, models, recommendations and high-value analyses.</p></article>
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Data Analyst</h3><p>Produce operational insights, monitor indicators and support day-to-day decision-making.</p></article>
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Data Journalist</h3><p>Tell engaging, verifiable and visual stories from well-documented data.</p></article>
      <article class="role-card"><h3>Freelancer</h3><p>Offer punctual and adaptable expertise across part or all of the data science cycle.</p></article>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" aria-labelledby="tools-title">
    <div class="resource-section__header">
      <h2 id="tools-title">Tools to Install</h2>
      <p>These tools form the minimal course environment.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="resource-hub-grid compact-hub">
      <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>R</h3><p>The language used to import, transform, visualize and analyze data.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://www.r-project.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>R Project</span><span>Official download.</span></a></div></article>
      <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>RStudio</h3><p>The working environment used to write code, manage projects and produce reports.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>RStudio Desktop</span><span>Download from Posit.</span></a></div></article>
      <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Quarto</h3><p>The system that turns .qmd files into HTML reports, notes and web pages.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Quarto get started</span><span>Installation and first document.</span></a></div></article>
      <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Git and GitHub</h3><p>Version-control tools used to track changes and submit some work.</p><div class="resource-link-list"><a href="https://git-scm.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>Git</span><span>Local installation.</span></a><a href="https://docs.github.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span>GitHub Docs</span><span>Official documentation.</span></a></div></article>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" aria-labelledby="routine-title">
    <div>
      <h2 id="routine-title">Minimal Routine</h2>
      <p>Each work session should follow a simple routine. It reduces errors and keeps the project reproducible.</p>
      <ol class="clean-steps">
        <li>Open the right project in RStudio.</li>
        <li>Read the learning-plan card linked to the task of the day.</li>
        <li>Run code in small sections and check the outputs.</li>
        <li>Render the Quarto document to catch errors.</li>
        <li>Keep only useful files, then commit if the module requires it.</li>
      </ol>
    </div>
    <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Help during the course">
      <article class="resource-compact"><h3>When you are stuck</h3><p>Reproduce the error, read the full message, then isolate the smallest possible example.</p></article>
      <article class="resource-compact"><h3>With the course AI</h3><p>Ask for an explanation, a check or a debugging lead. Always verify the answer before using it.</p></article>
      <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Before submitting</h3><p>Render the file, reread the conclusions and check that the deliverable answers the challenge.</p></article>
    </div>
  </section>
</div>
```
